title.rendered: I Am the Good Shepherd: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” A morning devotional on the Shepherd who knows you by name.

content.rendered:
I am the Good Shepherd. The Good Shepherd gives His life for the sheep. Not a hired hand who runs when the wolf appears. The Good Shepherd. The One who lays down His life for those who belong to Him.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, August 24, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep.”
John 10:11 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

John 10 reaches for the most familiar image in the ancient world of Israel. The shepherd and the sheep. Every hearer of Jesus that day had watched a shepherd walk a hillside, count his flock at nightfall, drive off predators, carry an injured lamb home on his shoulders. Into that familiar picture Jesus places a shocking claim. “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep.” Not a shepherd. Not one shepherd among many. The Good Shepherd. Distinct in kind, not just in degree.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of the claim: “I am the Good Shepherd who lays down my life as a sacrifice for the sheep” (John 10:11 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I am the Good Shepherd. The Good Shepherd risks and lays down His [own] life for the sheep” (John 10:11 AMPC). Risks. Lays down. The Good Shepherd does not calculate whether the sheep are worth the risk. He gives His life because they are His.

Jesus draws the contrast sharply in the very next verses. “He who is a hireling and not the shepherd, one who does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf catches the sheep and scatters them. The hireling flees because he is a hireling and does not care about the sheep” (John 10:12-13 NKJV). The hired hand serves the paycheque. When the wolf comes, the paycheque is not worth dying for. The sheep are on their own. But Jesus is not a hired hand. The sheep are His. And He does not run.

Then Jesus says something so intimate it should stop us in our tracks. “I am the good shepherd; and I know My sheep, and am known by My own” (John 10:14 NKJV). Not knows about. Knows. The Greek word Jesus uses is ginōskō. Intimate, experiential, personal knowledge. Not the knowledge of a database entry. The knowledge of a shepherd who has walked every hill with every sheep in his flock. He knows your name. He knows your voice. He knows the specific wolf circling your life this week. Not the crowd. You.

And in the fullness of time, the Good Shepherd did exactly what He said He would do. The wolf came at Calvary. The Shepherd stood His ground. The life He laid down purchased the flock forever. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you belong to a Good Shepherd who has already died for you. The rescue is paid. The wolf is defeated. Listen for His voice today above the other voices. Follow where He leads. He is trustworthy, and the sheep who know Him have nothing to fear.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is my Good Shepherd. He has laid down His life for me. He knows my name. He calls me by name. I am not a random member of a distant flock. I am His, personally, particularly, individually. I refuse to follow the voice of the stranger today. I listen for the voice of the One who has already died for me. I follow where He leads, confident that the Shepherd who gave His life for me will never abandon me in the pasture. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is my Good Shepherd. He knows me by name. He has laid down His life for me. I follow His voice today, above every other voice. I am His, and He is mine.
